children: Gold rises in early Asian trade, as markets weigh a pullback in oil prices. Softer energy prices could temper inflation concerns and ease pressure on yields, providing some support to gold, Infinox's Thadeu Dos Santos says in a note. However, the interest rate backdrop remains challenging and leaves the precious metal vulnerable to renewed selling pressure, the regional director says. Investors will focus on this week's U.S. inflation data for clues on the Fed's next interest rate move. A higher-interest-rate environment typically weighs on non-interest yielding assets such as gold. Spot gold is up 0.4% at $4,209.39 an ounce.(amanda.lee@wsj.com)
